note: No HANDOFF.json pre-existed in this sandbox at the start of this rework session; this file was created fresh rather than appended to, per the review_disposition/redesign requirement.

prior_attempts_rejected: Curated DENY-LIST at the command-runner boundary (src/specify_cli/tracker/gateway.py): _FORBIDDEN_SUBCOMMANDS/_FORBIDDEN_FLAGS/_FORBIDDEN_STATUS_VALUES matched against a canonicalized bd argv.
why_rejected: Two independent adversarial reviews REJECTED the deny-list: bd 1.2.2's real close-equivalent surface is larger than any hand-maintained blacklist -- `bd gate resolve` (bd's own --help: 'equivalent to bd close <gate-id>'), `bd epic close-eligible` (bulk-closes epics), `bd supersede --with` / `bd duplicate --of` / `bd duplicates --auto-merge` (auto-close their target), `bd delete --force` (permanent, worse than close), `bd merge-slot release`, `bd update --claim` (self-claim: sets assignee+status atomically), and `bd config set status.custom ...` were all found live against /opt/homebrew/bin/bd and none were on the prior blacklist.

Root defect: bd's done-category statuses are USER-CONFIGURABLE (`bd config set status.custom ...`), so a status-VALUE blacklist (_FORBIDDEN_STATUS_VALUES = {closed, done, tombstone}) is structurally incomplete -- it can never enumerate a caller-defined vocabulary. This is a category of bug a bigger blacklist cannot fix.
review_disposition.reviewers_explicit_recommendation: Invert to a deny-by-default ALLOW-LIST: enumerate the minimal set of bd operations the tracker adapter legitimately needs (read/query plus its actual non-lifecycle writes), deny everything else by construction, with no blacklist enumeration required for forward-compatibility against bd's future subcommands.

redesign.model: Deny-by-default allow-list matched on the FULL canonicalized subcommand path (not just argv[1]), plus an absolute (value-independent) flag-name ban for the two lifecycle-adjacent flags on the two allow-listed WRITE paths.
redesign.how_allowed_set_was_derived: Read the actual call sites in the landed TRK-M1-02/03 kernel (.sandboxes/TRK-M1-python-pedro.oWYyBQ/spec-kitty-tracker @ 6f65535, src/spec_kitty_tracker/connectors/beads.py): BeadsConnector.list_issues -> `list`, get_issue -> `show`, create_issue -> `create`, update_issue -> `update`, upsert_link -> `dep add`, add_comment -> `comments add`. This adapter is NOT read-only end-to-end (specify_cli/tracker/local_service.py drives BeadsConnector.create_issue/update_issue as part of two-way sync), so a read-only allow-list would have broken real, legitimate functionality; the allow-list instead names exactly these six paths and denies every other bd subcommand (assign, close/done, reopen, delete, gate *, epic *, supersede, duplicate(s), merge-slot *, config *, and anything bd adds in a future release) by construction.
redesign.lifecycle_flag_ban_rationale: This is a flag-NAME ban, not a value blacklist. bd's flag surface for create/update is fixed by the installed bd version (unlike its status *vocabulary*, which is user-configurable), so it does not carry the 'cannot be made complete' defect the prior status-value blacklist had. --status/-s is banned on `update` for EVERY value, including a superficially-safe non-terminal one (e.g. `in_progress`) -- the gateway cannot know, from a bare string, whether a given installation's `status.custom` config makes that value a done-category status. Any status transition is therefore treated as lifecycle and denied at this boundary; BeadsConnector's own A5 guard (TRK-M1-03) already restricts non-terminal-only status writes at the patch layer, and self-claim/lifecycle transitions remain host-owned via Spec Kitty's own claim/status flow, never via this raw bd-argv gateway.
redesign.subcommand_path_matching: _extract_subcommand_path() skips bd's root-level global flags (value-taking: --actor, --db, -C/--directory, --dolt-auto-commit; boolean: --json, --global, -h/--help, --ignore-schema-skew, --profile, -q/--quiet, --readonly, --sandbox, -v/--verbose, -V/--version -- enumerated live from `bd --help`), honors a literal `--` (pflag's stop-parsing marker) so a caller cannot hide the real subcommand behind it, and extends the path to a second token ONLY for the two compound parents that have an allow-listed two-word form (`dep`, `comments`) -- so `bd gate resolve` and a hypothetical `bd gate show` are both denied on the first token `gate` alone, without needing to separately deny every `gate` sub-subcommand.
redesign.canonicalize_argv: _canonicalize_argv() splits ANY glued `--flag=value` or single-character `-f=value` into the two-token shape -- generically, with no per-flag alias table -- so a caller cannot dodge the flag-name ban by picking the glued spelling. The deny check then names both the long and short spelling of each banned flag explicitly (no rewrite/alias step needed for the deny decision itself).
